oracle: Original IQ1 lattice initialization, native qsort, exhaustive weighted split fitting, neighbour search, scalar weighted/unweighted functions and reference wrappers compiled independently into iq1_oracle.dll.
qualifications: IQ1_S uses required explicit importance weights. IQ1_M has original optional-weight and unweighted paths; the latter uses squared input values as weights.
All weights are explicit when weighted. No importance weights are fabricated for the unweighted entry point. Zero-weight rows preserve source search/tie behavior.

The source iq1_find_best_neighbour2 exhaustive numerical fallback indexes xval by a grid index instead of a coordinate. Inputs whose neighbour scores cannot select a finite candidate are rejected atomically in Rust; undefined out-of-bounds reads are not reproduced.

native_qsort.qualification: Equal-value order is unspecified by C. This fixture pins the actual frozen MSVC UCRT comparator and tie ordering used for the IQ1 prefix sums.
native_qsort.rust_algorithm: Independent finite-value median-of-three partitioning, a maximum-selection short-range finish and trailing-pivot-tie pruning reproduce the actual native comparator ordering. SDK source was consulted to understand behavior; no vendor pointer-sort implementation is included in the Rust product.
